source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
The QTS Piscataway campus publishes 65 MW of IT capacity across two addresses on the same site. That figure places it first among New Jersey facilities by published IT load on this site, and it accounts for roughly 69 percent of the 94 MW total that this site has confirmed from operator spec pages across the state. The remaining 46 of 47 mapped New Jersey facilities publish no capacity figure, so the true state total is unknown and the ranking reflects only what operators have chosen to disclose.

At 40 kW per rack, a common assumption for AI training density, 65 MW of IT load translates to roughly 1,625 racks. At 10 kW per rack, a common assumption for general enterprise colocation, the same power supports roughly 6,500 racks. The operator does not publish a rack count, a cooling architecture, or a power usage effectiveness figure, so neither end of that range can be confirmed from available data. The gap between the two estimates is large enough that the campus's suitability for dense GPU workloads cannot be read from the published specifications alone.

The campus carries a LEED certification. LEED addresses the environmental performance of the building and its systems, not uptime tier or redundancy architecture, so this certification qualifies the campus as a recognized green building and nothing more specific to AI infrastructure. No tier classification, no tenant list, and no grid interconnection detail are published on the operator's spec page as read for this site.
